items.stem: A smart-city traffic project optimises only average vehicle speed and later finds pedestrian crossings became less safe. What lesson does this best illustrate?

options.text: Optimising a narrow metric can harm overall outcomes; goals and equity must be considered together
options.rationale: Correct: single-metric optimisation can produce harmful side effects without a broader view.

options.text: Smart cities should never measure anything
options.rationale: Measurement is useful; the issue is optimising too narrowly.

options.text: Pedestrians are irrelevant to mobility planning
options.rationale: Pedestrian safety is central to mobility outcomes.

options.text: Average speed is always the correct sole objective
options.rationale: A sole objective ignored safety and equity, which is the problem.

items.explanation: Correct: single-metric optimisation can produce harmful side effects without a broader view.

items.stem: Which TWO are legitimate concerns when deploying city-wide sensing? (Select TWO.)

options.text: Protecting residents' privacy and avoiding undue surveillance
options.rationale: Correct: pervasive sensing raises real privacy and surveillance concerns.

options.text: Ensuring equitable access so benefits are not limited to wealthy areas
options.rationale: Correct: equity of access is a key smart-city consideration.

options.text: Collecting as much personal data as possible with no purpose limit
options.rationale: Unlimited collection is a risk to avoid, not a goal.

options.text: Ignoring governance because the technology is new
options.rationale: Governance is more important, not less, for new systems.

items.explanation: Correct: pervasive sensing raises real privacy and surveillance concerns.

items.stem: What best distinguishes a genuinely 'smart' city system from simply installing technology?

options.text: Integrating sensing, data and services to improve outcomes for residents, with governance
options.rationale: Correct: smartness comes from integration and improved outcomes, not gadgets alone.

options.text: Having the largest number of cameras on every street
options.rationale: Counting devices is not what makes a city smart.

options.text: Replacing all public services with apps regardless of need
options.rationale: Blanket app replacement is not the definition of smart.

options.text: Keeping all city data secret from residents
options.rationale: Secrecy undermines engagement and trust, not a hallmark of smartness.

items.explanation: Correct: smartness comes from integration and improved outcomes, not gadgets alone.
